claim: Imaging-based neuroanatomical tracing identifies area-to-area or sparse neuron-to-neuron connectivity patterns, but with limited throughput.
source: Imaging-based neuroanatomical tracing identifies area-to-area or sparse neuron-to-neuron connectivity patterns, but with limited throughput.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities and limitations of imaging-based neuroanatomical tracing methods, presented as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Barcode-based connectomics maps large numbers of single-neuron projections, but remains a challenge for jointly analyzing single-cell transcriptomics.
source: Barcode-based connectomics maps large numbers of single-neuron projections, but remains a challenge for jointly analyzing single-cell transcriptomics.
evidence: This statement describes the capabilities and limitations of barcode-based connectomics methods, presented as established knowledge.

claim: MERGE-seq is a rAAV2-retro barcode-based multiplexed tracing method that simultaneously characterizes the projectome and transcriptome at the single neuron level.
source: Here, we established a rAAV2-retro barcode-based multiplexed tracing method that simultaneously characterizes the projectome and transcriptome at the single neuron level.
evidence: This is the primary methodological claim of the study, describing the development of MERGE-seq.

claim: MERGE-seq uncovered dedicated and collateral projection patterns of ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) neurons to five downstream targets.
source: We uncovered dedicated and collateral projection patterns of ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) neurons to five downstream targets
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 3.

claim: Projection-defined vmPFC neurons are molecularly heterogeneous.
source: and found that projection-defined vmPFC neurons are molecularly heterogeneous.
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis data presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 2.

claim: Pou3f1 is a marker gene enriched in neurons projecting to the lateral hypothalamus.
source: and verified Pou3f1 as a marker gene enriched in neurons projecting to the lateral hypothalamus
evidence: This claim is supported by both transcriptomic data and RNA FISH validation experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Pou3f1-expressing neurons represent a distinct subset with collateral projections to both dorsomedial striatum and lateral hypothalamus.
source: denoting a distinct subset with collateral projections to both dorsomedial striatum and lateral hypothalamus.
evidence: This claim is supported by dual-color retrograde tracing combined with RNA FISH data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Wiring diagrams of a brain can be divided into three levels: the macroscale connectome, the mesoscale connectome, and the microscale connectome.
source: Wiring diagrams of a brain can be divided into three levels: (1) the macroscale connectome that describes inter-areal connections, (2) the mesoscale connectome that describes connections between cells, and (3) the microscale connectome that describes connections at the synaptic level (Zeng, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zeng, 2018.

claim: Studying circuit architecture at the level of the mesoscale connectome describes how information flows between brain regions.
source: Studying circuit architecture at the level of the mesoscale connectome describes how information flows between brain regions (Oh et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oh et al., 2014.

claim: Neuroanatomical tracers are traditionally used to characterize regional connectivity matrices.
source: Traditionally, neuroanatomical tracers are used to characterize regional connectivity matrices (Cowan, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cowan, 1998.

claim: Recombinant virus-based tracers can be used in transgenic model organisms to obtain cell-type-specific connectivity.
source: To obtain cell-type-specific connectivity, one can use recombinant virus-based tracer in transgenic model organisms or more precisely trace a specific component of a neural circuit using viral-genetic tracing tools to dissect the input-output organization (Ghosh et al., 2011; Nassi et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ghosh et al., 2011; Nassi et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2015.

claim: Traditional viral-genetic tracing methods are highly reliant on complex recombinant virus design and genetically modified model organisms, and often are not at single-neuron resolution.
source: However, these methods are highly reliant on complex recombinant virus design and genetically modified model organism, and often are not at a single-neuron resolution.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of existing methods based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: High-throughput fluorescence imaging such as fMOST can reconstruct detailed neuron morphologies but requires specialized expertise and equipment and lacks transcriptomic information.
source: High-throughput fluorescence imaging, such as fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography (fMOST), can reconstruct detailed neuron morphologies but requires specialized expertise and equipment and lack transcriptomic information (Gong et al., 2016; Rompani et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gong et al., 2016; Rompani et al., 2017.

claim: MAPseq and BRICseq can only provide connectome information.
source: However, MAPseq and BRICseq can only provide connectome information (Huang et al., 2020; Kebschull et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 2020; Kebschull et al., 2016.

claim: BARseq is constrained to assessing a handful of genes via in situ hybridization.
source: BARseq is constrained to assessing a handful of genes via in situ hybridization (Chen et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019.

claim: ConnectID has low recovery of cells with dual connectome-transcriptome data (~16%, 391 cells with connectome barcode identity in 2450 cells with scRNA-seq).
source: and ConnectID has low recovery of cells with dual connectome-transcriptome data (~16%, 391 cells with connectome barcode identity in 2450 cells with scRNA-seq; Klingler et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Klingler et al., 2021.

claim: VECTORseq is limited by its number of transgenic barcodes used.
source: VECTORseq, a Retro-seq-based method (Tasic et al., 2018), is limited by its number of transgenic barcodes used (Cheung et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tasic et al., 2018 and Cheung et al., 2021.

claim: The updated BARseq protocol enables detection of up to 100 genes, but throughput remains lower and oligo synthesis costs remain higher compared to scRNA-seq.
source: The updated BARseq protocol enables detection of up to 100 genes, but throughput remains lower and oligo synthesis costs remain higher compared to scRNA-seq (Chen et al., 2023; Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2023; Sun et al., 2021.

claim: Existing methods fall short in efficiently integrating high-throughput projectomes and transcriptomes at the single-neuron level.
source: In summary, despite significant progress, existing methods fall short in efficiently integrating high-throughput projectomes and transcriptomes at the single-neuron level, hindering a comprehensive understanding of the connectomic and transcriptomic interplay in neuronal circuitry.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the review of existing methods and their limitations.

claim: Medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is involved in higher order cognitive functions, information processing (e.g., memory and emotions) and driving goal-directed actions.
source: Medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is an intricate brain region involved in higher order cognitive functions, information processing (e.g., memory and emotions) and driving goal-directed actions (Le Merre et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Le Merre et al., 2021.

claim: mPFC neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens encoding punishment-related internal states are located in more superficial layer 5a.
source: For example, mPFC neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens encoding punishment-related internal states were located in more superficial layer 5a, and mPFC neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area encoding aversive learning were located in deeper layer 5b (Kim et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2021.

claim: mPFC neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area encoding aversive learning are located in deeper layer 5b.
source: For example, mPFC neurons projecting to the nucleus accumbens encoding punishment-related internal states were located in more superficial layer 5a, and mPFC neurons projecting to the ventral tegmental area encoding aversive learning were located in deeper layer 5b (Kim et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2021.

claim: mPFC neurons can send collateral axons to multiple brain regions.
source: The answer to these questions may be further complicated by the finding that mPFC neurons can send collateral axons to multiple brain regions (Cornwall and Phillipson, 1988).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cornwall and Phillipson, 1988.

claim: MERGE-seq injected five rAAV2-retro viruses with distinct barcodes into five known downstream targets of vmPFC (AI, DMS, BLA, MD, and LH) in the same mouse brain.
source: We injected five rAAV2-retro viruses with distinct barcodes into the five known downstream targets of ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), including agranular insular cortex (AI), dorsomedial striatum (DMS), basolateral amygdala (BLA), mediodorsal thalamic nucleus (MD), and lateral hypothalamus (LH), in the same mouse brain such that each target region received a unique barcoded rAAV2-retro.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the MERGE-seq method.

claim: vmPFC neurons projecting to each downstream target are heterogeneous, composed of transcriptionally different subtypes of neurons.
source: We found that vmPFC neurons projecting to each downstream target are heterogeneous, which are composed of transcriptionally different subtypes of neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Approximately 65% of barcoded vmPFC neurons exhibited dedicated projection patterns, sending axonal projections exclusively to one of the five selected targets.
source: Approximately 65% of barcoded vmPFC neurons exhibited dedicated projection patterns based on MERGE-seq data, sending axonal projections exclusively to one of the five selected targets.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of projection patterns shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Approximately 35% of barcoded vmPFC neurons sent collateral projections to multiple brain regions, most of which are dual-target projection neurons (bifurcated projection).
source: Approximately 35% of barcoded vmPFC neurons sent collateral projections to multiple brain regions, most of which are dual-target projection neurons (bifurcated projection).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of projection patterns shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Layer 5 Pou3f1+ neurons collateralize between DMS and LH.
source: Additionally, dual-modal interrogation using RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and dual-color retrograde AAV labeling allowed us to confirm vmPFC neuron bifurcations to DMS and LH, demonstrating layer 5 Pou3f1+ neurons collateralize between these targets.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH and dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The rAAV2-retro viral vector was modified by adding a 15 bp barcode index and polyadenylation signal sequences to the 3' end of the EGFP sequences, driven by a short CAG promoter.
source: In order to use the 10x Genomics scRNA-seq system to analyze transcripts from cells infected with rAAV2-retro virus, we modified the viral vector by adding a 15 bp barcode index and polyadenylation signal sequences to the 3' end of the EGFP sequences, which was driven by a short CAG promoter (Figure 1A and B, see Materials and ethods).
evidence: This describes the design of the viral vector used in MERGE-seq, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A period of six weeks was set to allow efficient retrograde labeling of vmPFC neurons by barcoded viruses.
source: A period of six weeks was set to allow efficient retrograde labeling of vmPFC neurons by these barcoded viruses.
evidence: This describes the experimental timeline for viral labeling.

claim: 24,788 cells were detected in the raw data matrix.
source: We detected 24,788 cells in the raw data matrix.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the scRNA-seq experiment.

claim: Following quality control, 1791 cells from FACS and 19,470 single cells without sorting were recovered, totaling 21,261 cells.
source: Following initial quality control, which ensured the number of detected RNA in each cell ranged between 500 and 8000, RNA UMI counts in each cell were within 1000–60,000, and the percentage of mitochondrial genes remained below 20%, we recovered 1791 cells undergoing fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) from three mice and 19,470 single cells without sorting from the other three mice, a total of 21,261 cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the scRNA-seq experiment after quality control.

claim: Transcriptional profiling revealed major cell types including excitatory neurons (Slc17a7+), microglia (C1qa+), endothelial cells (Itm2a+), oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (Olig2+Mog-), oligodendrocyte (Olig2+Mog+), inhibitory neurons (Gad1+), astrocyte (Aldh1l1+), and activated microglia (C1qa+Pf4+).
source: Transcriptional profiling of all cells revealed major cell types including excitatory neurons (Slc17a7+), microglia (C1qa+), endothelial cells (Itm2a+, Endo), oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (Olig2+Mog-, OPCs), oligodendrocyte (Olig2+Mog+, Oligo), inhibitory neurons (Gad1+), astrocyte (Aldh1l1+, Astro), and activated microglia (C1qa+Pf4+, Act. Microglia) as previously reported (Bhattacherjee et al., 2019; Figure 1C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptomic clustering data shown in Figure 1C-E and citation to Bhattacherjee et al., 2019.

claim: There are sufficient sequence differences to distinguish one barcode from others and identify the right barcode among five references during sequencing.
source: Next, we showed that there were sufficient sequence differences to distinguish one barcode from others and sufficient sequences difference to identify the right barcode among five references during sequencing (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Hamming distance analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Barcoded cells were primarily excitatory neurons rather than inhibitory neurons or non-neuronal cell types.
source: Across all detected cell types, barcoded cells were primarily excitatory neurons rather than inhibitory neurons or non-neuronal cell types (2116 validly barcoded in 8805 excitatory neurons, and 5 validly barcoded in 2738 endothelial cells, 3 validly barcoded in 1780 oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, 7 validly barcoded in 1773 oligodendrocytes, and 17 in 1420 inhibitory neurons, Figure 1F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of barcoded cell types shown in Figure 1F and G.

claim: mPFC projection neurons are excitatory.
source: This is consistent with the finding that mPFC projection neurons are excitatory (Gabbott et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gabbott et al., 2005.

claim: 49.0% of FAC-sorted and 18.7% of unsorted cells were classified as barcoded using stringent threshold.
source: Using this stringent threshold, 49.0% of FAC-sorted and 18.7% of unsorted cells were classified as barcoded (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the barcode classification analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: EGFP+ ratios were 81% for FAC-sorted and 26% on average for unsorted cells.
source: In parallel, we calculated EGFP+ ratios (nUMI of EGFP RNA >0) as 81% for FAC-sorted and 26% on average for unsorted cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the EGFP expression analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Seven excitatory neuron clusters were generated, including L2/3-Calb1 (4.1%), L2/3-Rorb (5.9%), L5-Bcl6 (3.3%), L5-Htr2c (3.9%), L5-S100b (11.6%), L6-Npy (12.6%), and L6-Syt6 (58.7%).
source: These neuron clusters include L2/3-Calb1 (4.1%), L2/3-Rorb (5.9%), L5-Bcl6 (3.3%), L5-Htr2c (3.9%), L5-S100b (11.6%), L6-Npy (12.6%), and L6-Syt6 (58.7%; Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by clustering analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: More layer 6 neurons were captured than superficial layer neurons (12.6% L6-Npy and 58.7% L6-Syt6).
source: Of note, we captured more layer 6 neurons than superficial layer neurons (12.6% L6-Npy and 58.7% L6-Syt6, Figure 2B), which is different from a previous report (Bhattacherjee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 2B, compared to a previous report.

claim: Different dissociation protocols may cause biased neuron capture.
source: We speculate that different dissociation protocols may cause biased neuron capture.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference in layer distribution.

claim: Cells that were retrogradely barcoded spanned all layers of the vmPFC (layer 2/3, 5, and 6) and included all seven neuronal subtypes.
source: Cells that were retrogradely barcoded spanned all layers of the vmPFC (layer 2/3, 5, and 6) and included all seven neuronal subtypes (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the distribution of barcoded cells across neuronal subtypes shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Excitatory neuronal subtypes were highly corresponding to the spatially resolved PFC excitatory neuronal subtypes.
source: These subtypes were highly corresponding to the spatially resolved PFC excitatory neuronal subtypes (Bhattacherjee et al., 2023; see Materials and methods, Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2D and citation to Bhattacherjee et al., 2023.

claim: Excitatory neuronal subtypes are transcriptionally similar to those previously reported.
source: We also found that excitatory neuronal subtypes are transcriptionally similar to those previously reported (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D; Bhattacherjee et al., 2019; Lui et al., 2021; Yao et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and citations to previous studies.

claim: Multiple viral infections will not significantly affect the transcriptional state of retrogradely labeled vmPFC neurons.
source: All these integrated analyses suggest that multiple viral infections will not significantly affect the transcriptional state of these retrogradely labeled vmPFC neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of transcriptional profiles to previously reported data.

claim: For the L5-Htr2c subtype, only nine neurons were recovered with valid barcodes, possibly due to cell loss during single-cell dissociation or tropism of AAV2-retro, or these neurons may intrinsically not project to any target chosen.
source: For the L5-Htr2c subtype, only nine neurons were recovered with valid barcodes, possibly due to cell loss during single-cell dissociation or tropism of AAV2-retro, or these neurons may intrinsically not project to any target we chose (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation with speculative explanations for the low recovery of L5-Htr2c neurons.

claim: Neurons projecting to DMS were abundant (n=1242), whereas neurons projecting to BLA were rare (n=163).
source: Neurons projecting to DMS were abundant (n=1242), whereas neurons projecting to BLA were rare (n=163; Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the projection analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The abundance of DMS-projecting and scarcity of BLA-projecting neurons are consistent with data acquired via conventional fluorescence-based retrograde tracing in the prefrontal cortex of rats.
source: These results are consistent with data acquired via conventional fluorescence-based retrograde tracing in the prefrontal cortex of rats (Gabbott et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gabbott et al., 2005.

claim: Target specific projection neurons were transcriptionally heterogeneous, composed of different neuronal subtypes.
source: Interestingly, we found that these target specific projection neurons were transcriptionally heterogeneous, which were composed of different neuronal subtypes (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the subtype composition analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Neurons projecting to LH or MD were mainly L6-Syt6 subtype.
source: Neurons projecting to LH or MD were mainly L6-Syt6 subtype, whereas neurons projecting to AI, DMS, or BLA were mainly composed of L5-S100b, and to a lesser extent L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb subtypes (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the subtype composition analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Neurons projecting to AI, DMS, or BLA were mainly composed of L5-S100b, and to a lesser extent L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb subtypes.
source: Neurons projecting to LH or MD were mainly L6-Syt6 subtype, whereas neurons projecting to AI, DMS, or BLA were mainly composed of L5-S100b, and to a lesser extent L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb subtypes (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the subtype composition analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Each transcriptome-defined neuron subtype can project to specific but multiple targets.
source: By calculating the projection properties of each vmPFC neuron subtype, we found that each transcriptome-defined neuron subtype can project to specific but multiple targets.
evidence: This claim is supported by the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: L5-S100b, L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb mainly projected to AI, DMS and BLA.
source: For instance, L5-S100b, L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb mainly projected to AI, DMS and BLA, while L6-Syt6 mainly projected to MD and LH (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: L6-Syt6 mainly projected to MD and LH.
source: For instance, L5-S100b, L6-Npy and L2/3-Rorb mainly projected to AI, DMS and BLA, while L6-Syt6 mainly projected to MD and LH (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Different neuron subtypes localized in the same layer could project to distinct targets.
source: Interestingly, we also found that different neuron subtypes localized in the same layer could project to distinct targets. For instance, L6-Npy neurons projecting to AI, DMS, and BLA, while L6-Syt6 neurons projecting to MD, DMS, and LH (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: 64.88% of 2050 viral-barcoded neurons belonged to dedicated projection and the remaining belonged to collateral projection.
source: We found 64.88% of 2050 viral-barcoded neurons belonged to dedicated projection and the remaining belonged to collateral projection.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 23.37% of barcoded neurons had dual targets (bifurcated projection), 8.15% had triple targets, and 3.61% projected to more than three targets.
source: A total of 23.37% had dual targets (bifurcated projection), 8.15% had triple targets, and 3.61%, if any, projected to more than three targets (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the projection pattern analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: vmPFC neurons projecting to AI or BLA were more likely to have collateral projection to DMS.
source: By calculating the conditional probability that the same neuron projects to two targets (see Materials and methods), we found that vmPFC neurons projecting to AI or BLA were more likely to have collateral projection to DMS (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by conditional probability analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There is a relatively high conditional probability of collateral projection between MD and LH, or DMS and LH, or DMS and MD.
source: We also observed a relatively high conditional probability of collateral projection between MD and LH, or DMS and LH, or DMS and MD (Figure 3B), suggesting bifurcated projections to these paired targets for single vmPFC neuron.
evidence: This claim is supported by conditional probability analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 17.8% ± 0.11% of vmPFC neurons collateralize to DMS and LH.
source: Consistent with MERGE-seq identifying DMS + LH bifurcated projections (Figure 3B), dual-color labeling revealed 17.8% ± 0.11% of vmPFC neurons collateralize to DMS and LH (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: 73.28% ± 7.60% of DMS + LH bifurcated neurons localized to layer 5.
source: Of these, 73.28% ± 7.60% localized to layer 5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by layer distribution analysis of dual-color labeled neurons shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: 23.1% ± 2.03% of dual-color neurons showed DMS + AI bifurcated projection.
source: These patterns included DMS + AI (23.1% ± 2.03% of all dual-color neurons) and DMS + BLA (6.59% ± 1.55%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-I.

claim: 6.59% ± 1.55% of dual-color neurons showed DMS + BLA bifurcated projection.
source: These patterns included DMS + AI (23.1% ± 2.03% of all dual-color neurons) and DMS + BLA (6.59% ± 1.55%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-I.

claim: Only 1.66% ± 0.92% of dual-color labeled neurons were observed in BLA + LH group.
source: In contrast, we only observed 1.66% ± 0.92% of dual-color labeled neurons in BLA + LH group (Figure 3—figure supplement 1J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1J-L.

claim: DMS, AI + DMS, MD, and LH projection patterns appear as the most frequent projection patterns in both MERGE-seq and fMOST studies.
source: We found that DMS, AI + DMS, MD, and LH projection pattern appear as the most frequent projection patterns in both studies, with a relatively higher percentage of DMS dedicated projection pattern in MERGE-seq data (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of MERGE-seq and fMOST data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There were no significant differences in projection pattern percentages between MERGE-seq and fMOST when categorized by number of targets.
source: We further categorized projection patterns by number of targets and found no significant differences versus imaging-based reconstruction (Figure 3D), indicating MERGE-seq faithfully identifies projection patterns.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Dedicated and collateral projection neurons were largely transcriptionally diverse (≥3 subtypes).
source: While dedicated and collateral projection neurons were largely transcriptionally diverse (≥3 subtypes, Figure 3G), certain projections like MD-projecting and DMS + MD-projecting were highly homogeneous, composed of >90% L6-Syt6 cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell type composition analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: MD-projecting and DMS + MD-projecting neurons were highly homogeneous, composed of >90% L6-Syt6 cells.
source: While dedicated and collateral projection neurons were largely transcriptionally diverse (≥3 subtypes, Figure 3G), certain projections like MD-projecting and DMS + MD-projecting were highly homogeneous, composed of >90% L6-Syt6 cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell type composition analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Syt6, Foxp2, and Cyr61 are both MD-projecting DEGs and marker genes of L6-Syt6 neurons.
source: For example, Syt6, Foxp2, and Cyr61 are both MD-projecting DEGs and marker genes of L6-Syt6 neurons; Rorb and Slc24a3 are both DMS-projecting DEGs and marker genes of layer 2/3 neurons (neuronal subtype L2/3-Rorb; Figure 2C, Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 4A and marker gene expression in Figure 2C.

claim: Rorb and Slc24a3 are both DMS-projecting DEGs and marker genes of layer 2/3 neurons (neuronal subtype L2/3-Rorb).
source: For example, Syt6, Foxp2, and Cyr61 are both MD-projecting DEGs and marker genes of L6-Syt6 neurons; Rorb and Slc24a3 are both DMS-projecting DEGs and marker genes of layer 2/3 neurons (neuronal subtype L2/3-Rorb; Figure 2C, Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and marker gene expression in Figure 2C.

claim: About 51.6% ± 16.9% Syt6+ neurons project to MD.
source: By retrograde labeling of MD-projecting neurons and Syt6 FISH experiment, we found that about 51.6% ± 16.9% Syt6+ neurons project to MD.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH and retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: Among Syt6+ MD-projecting neurons, 84.2% ± 14.8% were located in layer 6 while 15.8% ± 14.8% were located in layer 5.
source: Further statistical analysis showed that, among Syt6+ MD-projecting (Syt6+EGFP+) neurons, 84.2% ± 14.8% were located in layer 6 while 15.8% ± 14.8% were located in layer 5 (Figure 4C)
evidence: This claim is supported by layer distribution analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: DEGs were rare in comparisons between projection patterns A/B vs. A, or A/B vs. B in all groups tested, except for the DMS + LH group and DMS + MD group.
source: Next, we asked whether there was transcriptional difference between neurons with dedicated projection to A and neurons with bifurcated projection to A and B. DEGs were rare in comparisons between projection patterns A/B vs. A, or A/B vs. B in all of groups we tested, except for the DMS + LH group and DMS + MD group (Figure 5B and C,Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 5B-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: DMS + LH projection neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to LH.
source: We found that DMS + LH projection neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to LH, and DMS + MD neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to MD (Figure 5B and C,Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: DMS + MD neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to MD.
source: We found that DMS + LH projection neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to LH, and DMS + MD neurons were transcriptionally distinct to DMS but similar to MD (Figure 5B and C,Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pou3f1, Igfbp4, and Gprc5b are differentially expressed in DMS + LH projection neurons.
source: Specifically, we identified a set of genes which differentially expressed in DMS + LH projection neurons (such as Pou3f1, Igfbp4, and Gprc5b) or DMS + MD projection neurons (such as Rprm, Crym, Hs3st4 and Bc1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Rprm, Crym, Hs3st4 and Bc1 are differentially expressed in DMS + MD projection neurons.
source: Specifically, we identified a set of genes which differentially expressed in DMS + LH projection neurons (such as Pou3f1, Igfbp4, and Gprc5b) or DMS + MD projection neurons (such as Rprm, Crym, Hs3st4 and Bc1).
evidence: This claim is supported by DEG analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pou3f1 is a marker gene of L5-Bcl6 neurons.
source: Interestingly, Pou3f1 is marker gene of L5-Bcl6 neurons (layer 5 neuron subtype), representing one of the two distinct neuron subtypes within the DMS + LH projection neuronal population (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by marker gene analysis and cell type composition shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The expression of Pou3f1 was mainly distributed in layer 5.
source: We found that the expression of Pou3f1 was mainly distributed in layer 5, where Pou3f1 was specifically expressed in dual-color labeled DMS + LH projecting neurons (white arrowheads, Figure 5E) and LH projecting neurons (white arrows, Figure 5E), but not DMS projecting neurons (blue arrows, Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: Pou3f1 was specifically expressed in dual-color labeled DMS + LH projecting neurons and LH projecting neurons, but not DMS projecting neurons.
source: We found that the expression of Pou3f1 was mainly distributed in layer 5, where Pou3f1 was specifically expressed in dual-color labeled DMS + LH projecting neurons (white arrowheads, Figure 5E) and LH projecting neurons (white arrows, Figure 5E), but not DMS projecting neurons (blue arrows, Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH and dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Among Pou3f1+ neurons, there are 55.7% ± 10.4% DMS + LH-projecting neurons, 31.6% ± 13.1% dedicated LH-projecting neurons, and 8.89% ± 2.38% dedicated DMS-projecting neurons.
source: Quantification analysis showed that, among Pou3f1+ neurons, there are 55.7% ± 10.4% DMS + LH-projecting (Pou3f1+EGFP+tdT+) neurons, 31.6% ± 13.1% dedicated LH-projecting (Pou3f1+EGFP-tdT+) neurons, and 8.89% ± 2.38% dedicated DMS-projecting (Pou3f1+EGFP+tdT-) neurons (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of RNA FISH and dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: 3.79% ± 2.91% of Pou3f1+ neurons did not project to either DMS or LH.
source: We additionally discovered that 3.79% ± 2.91% of Pou3f1+ neurons did not project to either DMS or LH (Pou3f1+EGFP-tdT-) (yellow arrowheads, Figure 5F, Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification of RNA FISH and dual-color retrograde tracing data shown in Figure 5F-G.

claim: Using top 50 HVGs for modeling yielded the highest F1 score, AUC, and a comparatively high prediction accuracy.
source: This analysis revealed that employing the top 50 HVGs for modeling yielded the the highest F1 score (a harmonic mean of precision and recall), area under the curve (AUC), and a comparatively high prediction accuracy (see Materials and methods, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning model performance analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Using top 50 HVGs gave rise to significantly better model performance compared to using randomly chosen 50 genes.
source: Using top 50 HVGs also gave rise to significantly better model performance in regarding to prediction accuracy, AUC and F1 score, compared to using randomly chosen 50 genes (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning model comparison shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Randomly swapping barcoded with non-barcoded labels substantially decreased model predictive performance.
source: We also performed 100 iterations randomly sampling 1000 cells and swapping barcoded with non-barcoded labels, which substantially decreased model predictive performance across various evaluation metrics (see Materials and methods, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by label swapping analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Nptxr gene was the top positive predictor for DMS projection.
source: As examples, Nptxr gene was the top positive predictors for DMS projection, suggesting that a cell that expresses high levels of Nptxr has a higher probability of projecting to DMS.
evidence: This claim is supported by SHAP analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Rprm was the top positive predictor for MD projection.
source: Similarly, Rprm was the top positive predictors for MD projection.
evidence: This claim is supported by SHAP analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The expression pattern of top effective genes mostly overlaps with projection barcode distribution.
source: By examining top effective genes (features) on PC embeddings of the projection matrix, we found that the expression pattern of these positive predictors mostly overlaps with projection barcode distribution (Figure 6D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of gene expression and barcode distribution shown in Figure 6D and F.

claim: MAPseq mainly focuses on elucidating the projections of individual neurons in a single brain without providing the transcriptional signatures corresponding to those individual neurons.
source: Early approaches of barcode-based neuronal projection mapping mainly focus on elucidating the projections of individual neurons in a single brain without providing the transcriptional signatures corresponding to those individual neurons (MAPseq; Kebschull et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kebschull et al., 2016.

claim: BARseq can acquire single-neuron transcriptome and projectome, but with only a limited number of genes due to limited throughput of in situ sequencing.
source: BARseq can acquire single-neuron transcriptome and projectome, but with only a number of genes due to limited throughout of in situ sequencing.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of BARseq based on established knowledge.

claim: An improved version of BARseq can allow tens of genes to be detected, but still with a low throughput compared to scRNA-seq and a high cost in regards to synthesizing RNA probes.
source: An improved version of BARseq can allow tens of genes to be detected, but still with a low throughput compared to scRNA-seq and a high cost in regards to synthesizing RNA probes (Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2021.

claim: ConnectID improves the detection of transcriptome using scRNA-seq but has a relatively low recovery rate of cells with transcriptome and projectome simultaneously (~16%).
source: ConnectID (scRNA-seq combined with MAPseq) improves the detection of transcriptome using scRNA-seq but has a relatively low recovery rate of cells with transcriptome and projectome simultaneously (~16%, 391 cells with barcode identity in 2450 cells with scRNA-seq; Klingler et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Klingler et al., 2021.

claim: MERGE-seq enables transcriptional profiling of thousands of genes per neuron, with valid projectome barcode information recovered from approximately 50% of FAC-sorted cells.
source: In contrast, MERGE-seq enables transcriptional profiling of thousands of genes per neuron, with valid projectome barcode information recovered from approximately 50% of FAC-sorted cells passing stringent determination criteria.
evidence: This is a summary of MERGE-seq performance based on the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In BARseq or ConnectID, users need to perform numerous tissue homogenization and sequencing for downstream brain regions to query target area barcodes information.
source: While, in BARseq or ConnectID, users need to perform numerous tissue homogenization and sequencing for downstream brain regions to query target area barcodes information (projection).
evidence: This is a statement about the workflow requirements of BARseq and ConnectID based on established knowledge.

claim: Previous retro-AAV techniques have not developed a multiplexed approach for investigating the complex collateral projection patterns of neurons.
source: Previous research has employed retro-AAV techniques to probe the projection-specific transcriptome or epigenome of individual neurons (Lui et al., 2021; Tasic et al., 2018; Tasic et al., 2016; Yao et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021). Yet, these studies have not developed a multiplexed approach for investigating the complex collateral projection patterns of neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and assessment of their limitations.

claim: VECTORseq used several viral transgenes including three recombinases (DreO, Cre, Flpo) and two fluorescent proteins (tdTomato and EGFP) to barcode neurons.
source: VECTORseq used several viral transgenes including three recombinases (DreO, Cre, Flpo) and two fluorescent proteins (tdTomato and EGFP) to barcode neurons.
evidence: This is a description of the VECTORseq method based on established knowledge.

claim: VECTORseq transgenes are variable in length and driven by different promoters with different strength.
source: However, these transgenes are variable in length (DreO, ~1000 bp; Cre, ~1000 bp; FLPo, ~1200 bp; tdTomato, ~1400 bp; EGFP, ~700 bp) and driven by different promoters with different strength (EF1a, hSyn, CAG).
evidence: This is a description of the VECTORseq method based on established knowledge.

claim: Differential expression of different transgenes in VECTORseq will inevitably result in different rates of transgene recovery in labeled neurons.
source: Such an approach will inevitably result in differential expression of these different transgenes in labelled neurons, which in turn leads to different rates of transgene recovery in these neurons.
evidence: This is an inference about the consequences of using different transgenes in VECTORseq.

claim: Viral-mediated overexpression of recombinases may lead to toxicity in labeled neurons due to non-specific recombination events.
source: In addition, viral-mediated overexpression of these recombinase may lead to toxic to the labeled neurons due to non-specific recombination events (Xiao et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xiao et al., 2012.

claim: MERGE-seq used 15-nucleotide barcode sequences in the 3'UTR region of EGFP as projection index driven by the same promoter to label different projection neurons.
source: In contrast, MERGE-seq used 15-nucleotide barcode sequences in the 3'UTR region of EGFP as projection index driven by the same promoter to label different projection neurons.
evidence: This describes the design of MERGE-seq barcodes.

claim: The expression of different barcoded EGFP mRNA in MERGE-seq is comparable.
source: The expression of these different barcoded EGFP mRNA is comparable, and the number of these barcoded retro-AAV is unlimited.
evidence: This is a statement about the design advantage of MERGE-seq.

claim: MERGE-seq allows users to examine more populations (theoretically unlimited) in one brain and more extensive analysis of collateralization.
source: Therefore, MERGE-seq allows users to examine more populations (theoretically unlimited) in one brain and more extensive analysis of collateralization.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of MERGE-seq based on its design.

claim: The collateral projection patterns of single neurons were not reported in VECTORseq and Retro-seq-based methods.
source: However, the collateral projection patterns of single neurons were not reported in VECTORseq and Retro-seq-based method (Cheung et al., 2021; Lui et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cheung et al., 2021 and Lui et al., 2021.

claim: Lui et al., 2021 used Retro-seq to investigate the correspondence between transcriptomics and projection patterns of vmPFC neurons, and inferred collateral projection based on population level multi-target projections.
source: For example, Lui et al., 2021. used Retro-seq to investigate the correspondence between transcriptomics and projection patterns of vmPFC neurons, and inferred collateral projection based on the finding that transcriptome-defined neuron subtypes can project to different targets (or neurons projecting to different targets share common transcriptome-defined neuron subtype).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lui et al., 2021.

claim: Population level multi-target projections of a transcriptome-defined neuron subtype do not necessarily reflect collateral projection of individual neurons within a subtype.
source: However, the population level multi-target projections of a transcriptome-defined neuron subtype do not necessarily reflect collateral projection of individual neurons within a subtype.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of population-level analysis.

claim: Individual neurons within a subtype could project to distinct targets (dedicated projection), but their collective projections show multiple targets.
source: For instance, individual neurons within a subtype could project to distinct targets (dedicated projection), but their collective projections show multiple targets.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of population-level analysis.

claim: MERGE-seq strategy can be readily applied to other animal models, which is especially beneficial for research in models where genetic manipulation is challenging.
source: In addition, MERGE-seq strategy can be readily applied to other animal models, which is especially beneficial for research in models (e.g. non-human primate) where genetic manipulation is challenging.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of MERGE-seq.

claim: Retro-seq methods provide valuable population-level insights but do not capture the complex collateral projections that MERGE-seq can discern at the single-cell level.
source: In summary, while Retro-seq methods provide valuable population-level insights, they do not capture the complex collateral projections that MERGE-seq can discern at the single-cell level.
evidence: This is a summary statement comparing MERGE-seq to Retro-seq methods.

claim: Individual neurons within transcriptome-defined subtypes exhibit a diverse range of projection patterns.
source: Our findings build upon and extend those of Lui et al. by demonstrating that individual neurons within transcriptome-defined subtypes exhibit a diverse range of projection patterns.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from MERGE-seq analysis.

claim: MERGE-seq does not offer spatial information of neurons currently.
source: Although MERGE-seq does not offer spatial information of neurons currently, it leverages widely accessible droplet-based scRNA-seq, avoiding specialized equipment.
evidence: This is a statement about the current limitations of MERGE-seq.

claim: Extensive spatially resolved mouse brain atlases allow for easy spatial annotation of cell populations using DEGs identified by scRNA-seq.
source: Meanwhile, the extensive spatially resolved mouse brain atlases available (Allen et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023) allow for easy spatial annotation of cell populations using DEGs identified by scRNA-seq, as we demonstrated by mapping neuronal subtypes with MERFISH data of PFC.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Allen et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023 and demonstration in the manuscript.

claim: A recognized limitation of using retro-AAV-based methods is the imperfect retrograde labeling efficiency in target regions.
source: First, a recognized limitation of using retro-AAV-based methods, including MERGE-seq, is the imperfect retrograde labeling efficiency in target regions.
evidence: This is a statement about a known limitation of retro-AAV methods.

claim: Labeling efficiency could be variable depending on different source brain regions, projection strength, the distance between source and target brain regions and different AAV serotypes or tropism.
source: Labeling efficiency could be variable depending on the different source brain regions, projection strength, the distance between source and target brain regions and different AAV serotypes or tropism.
evidence: This is a statement about factors affecting labeling efficiency based on established knowledge.

claim: Single-cell dissociation for scRNA-seq can result in cell loss, thereby reducing the recovery rate of barcoded neurons.
source: Furthermore, single-cell dissociation for scRNA-seq can result in cell loss, thereby reducing the recovery rate of barcoded neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about a known limitation of scRNA-seq methods.

claim: The quantitative conclusions drawn from MERGE-seq might not fully represent the true extent of neuronal projections.
source: Consequently, the quantitative conclusions drawn here might not fully represent the true extent of neuronal projections.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the method.

claim: The robust detection of projection barcodes and its recovery rate in neurons labeled with barcoded AAV-retro viruses is a critical and challenging aspect of MERGE-seq methodology.
source: Second, the robust detection of projection barcodes and its recovery rate in neurons labeled with barcoded AAV-retro viruses is indeed a critical and challenging aspect of our methodology.
evidence: This is a statement about a challenge in the MERGE-seq methodology.

claim: Differential viral transduction efficiency across neurons leads to inconsistent barcode expression.
source: As mentioned above, this challenge is largely due to the differential viral transduction efficiency across neurons, leading to inconsistent barcode expression.
evidence: This is a statement about a factor affecting barcode detection.

claim: Neurons with low barcode expression may fall beneath the detection threshold of conventional sequencing methods.
source: Neurons with low barcode expression may fall beneath the detection threshold of conventional sequencing methods.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of sequencing methods.

claim: A suboptimal recovery rate can potentially lead to underrepresentation of certain neuron populations or projection patterns in the analyzed data.
source: A suboptimal recovery rate can potentially lead to underrepresentation of certain neuron populations or projection patterns in the analyzed data.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential consequences of low recovery rate.

claim: The retrograde transport of AAV has been effectively demonstrated to target projection neurons at axonal terminals.
source: However, the retrograde transport of AAV has been effectively demonstrated to target projection neurons at axonal terminals, with injections into the DMS exhibiting labeling patterns and efficiencies that match those of synthetic tracers (Tervo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tervo et al., 2016.

claim: AAV2 spread is confined to the vicinity of synaptic terminals and does not affect axon fibers in passages.
source: Further, it has been experimentally verified that AAV2 spread is confined to the vicinity of synaptic terminals and does not affect axon fibers in passages, especially as evidenced by retro-AAV injections in the cervical spinal cord (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2018.
